title: Code quality judgements
description: does documentation and code align? is a method too long given a specified max length? categorize cyclomatic complexity; does a test actually test the intended behavior? are important branches untested? what will the code return? will it produce the declared schema? does it call external functions? is it side-effect free? does it mutate state? arbitrary-code-execution potential? should this code be optimized or is optimization unlikely to matter? does it need explanatory comments? does it require a live datasource? browser/server/both? memory/CPU/GPU intensity; thread safety; blocking behavior; command destructiveness; estimated runtime class; programming-language identification; application-domain classification.

title: Program-behavior prediction
description: given short code, predict output, exception, state mutation, filesystem/network effects, stdout/stderr, exit status, returned type, number of iterations, whether execution terminates; classic interview-style traps but also realistic application code.

title: Code requirement satisfaction
description: given a natural-language task and candidate implementation, decide which requirements are actually implemented, partially implemented, contradicted, or absent; distinguish superficial keyword matches from behavioral compliance.

title: Patch/diff correctness
description: given original code, requested change and patch, decide whether the patch actually solves the request; identify unrelated behavior changes, regressions, incomplete modifications, stale tests, obsolete branches.

title: Test quality and adequacy
description: does the test exercise the behavior named by its title? can it pass despite a broken implementation? does it test implementation details rather than contract? missing boundary conditions? duplicated tests? property/invariant that should be tested? score semantic coverage independently from line coverage.

title: API-contract compatibility
description: does client request match server contract? path/method/header/content-type mismatch; required vs optional fields; return shape; pagination contract; sync/async mismatch; REST/OpenAPI/GraphQL/RPC examples; backwards compatibility.

title: Dependency/API existence judgements
description: does the referenced method plausibly belong to the named library/version? candidate calls from documentation vs fabricated APIs; deprecated methods; package-name confusion; stdlib vs third-party dependency; import-path compatibility.

title: Version compatibility
description: given dependency/runtime versions and feature usage, decide compatible/incompatible/unknown; Python/Node/Rust/Java versions, CUDA/runtime pairs, database versions, browser features, serialization formats.

title: Environment/portability judgements
description: browser-only, Node-only, POSIX-only, Windows-specific, GPU-required, CUDA-specific, root-required, interactive-terminal-dependent, filesystem-dependent, locale-dependent, architecture-dependent, isomorphic.

title: Concurrency correctness
description: race conditions, shared mutable state, atomicity assumptions, lock ordering, possible deadlock, async misuse, reentrancy, thread safety, process safety, duplicate-job execution.

title: Idempotency judgements
description: HTTP retries, payment processing, migration scripts, queue consumers, file transformations: can repeated execution alter the outcome incorrectly? distinguish read-only, naturally idempotent, explicitly idempotent and non-idempotent operations.

title: Error-handling quality
description: exception swallowed? retry useful or harmful? retryable vs permanent failure; cleanup guaranteed? fallback masks corruption? error loses useful context? timeout required? failure leaves inconsistent state?

title: Algorithm/data-structure appropriateness
description: list vs hash map vs tree vs heap; full sort vs top-k; linear scan vs indexed lookup; algorithm asymptotically inappropriate? optimization justified by expected input sizes?

title: Complexity estimation
description: categorize time/memory complexity; distinguish worst/average/amortized; identify input variable controlling complexity; detect accidental quadratic behavior; score practical rather than merely asymptotic cost.

title: Performance-bottleneck attribution
description: given code plus timings, identify CPU, I/O, memory bandwidth, network, lock contention, serialization, database, accelerator or startup bottleneck; decide whether proposed optimization affects the bottleneck.

title: Parallelization suitability
description: is the task embarrassingly parallel? state synchronization needed? batchable? vectorizable? GPU-friendly? multiprocessing useful? parallelism likely slower because workload is tiny?

title: Database-query reasoning
description: SQL result semantics, incorrect joins, duplicate rows, missing predicates, NULL semantics, aggregation correctness, N+1 queries, index usefulness, transaction isolation assumptions.

title: Regex/pattern correctness
description: does regex accept/reject supplied examples? catastrophic-backtracking potential; anchored vs substring matching; Unicode assumptions; overly broad/overly strict validation.

title: State-machine correctness
description: given states/events/transitions, is a transition legal? unreachable states? missing terminal state? event sequence impossible? transition introduces invariant violation?

title: Serialization compatibility
description: JSON/JSONL/YAML/CSV/Protobuf-like representations; numeric/string coercion, enum incompatibilities, absent/null distinction, precision loss, ordering assumptions.

title: Data-migration correctness
description: old/new schema plus transformation: is information lost? reversible? duplicate creation possible? migration safe to retry? values mapped to wrong enum/unit?

title: Distributed-systems consistency
description: event order, stale replicas, at-least-once delivery, duplicate messages, leader changes, eventual consistency; decide whether observed states are possible and whether invariants survive.

title: Cache correctness
description: stale cache, incorrect keying, tenant leakage, invalidation mistakes, TTL assumptions, cacheable vs non-cacheable responses, derived-data dependency changes.

title: Observability adequacy
description: given system behavior and logs/metrics/traces, decide whether evidence can distinguish likely failure modes; identify missing correlation IDs, timings, error context, cardinality problems.

title: Log/event-sequence diagnosis
description: given textual logs, decide most plausible execution path, component that failed first, causal vs downstream errors, whether retries recovered, whether timestamps violate expected ordering.

title: Configuration correctness
description: `Dockerfile`, Compose, Kubernetes, CI, package config, compiler config, environment variables represented as text; incompatible options, wrong paths, missing required keys, overridden values.

title: Command-line semantics
description: what does this pipeline actually do? destructive/non-destructive; local/network effects; blocking? requires stdin? can glob expand dangerously? expected output class; approximate runtime category.

title: Open-source/license compatibility
description: given licenses and distribution arrangement, classify likely compatibility/obligation category from supplied license rules; notice/source-distribution requirements; distinguish linking, copying and mere tool usage.

title: Accessibility semantics from source
description: HTML/ARIA/textual component representation: correct label association? keyboard reachable? heading hierarchy? interactive element role? duplicate labels? accessibility claim unsupported?

title: Graph logic
description: given reasoning/causal graph, judge whether edges are supported, merely correlated, impossible, circular, redundant or hallucinated; determine whether conclusion follows from reachable evidence.

title: Graph knowledge
description: given concept/entity graph, judge whether relation types are correct: `is-a`, `part-of`, `causes`, `located-in`, `authored-by`, `depends-on`; score semantic closeness of candidate edges.

title: Ontology/taxonomy consistency
description: dog→mammal valid, mammal→dog too specific; instance-vs-class mistakes; disjoint categories; transitive relationships; parent category chosen at wrong abstraction level.

title: Graph-path relevance
description: given query and a knowledge graph, rank possible paths by how directly they explain/connect the concepts; reject paths connected only through generic hubs.

title: Temporal graph consistency
description: edge valid only before/after date X; employment, ownership, dependency/version, historical relationships; detect relations impossible simultaneously.

title: Causal-chain validation
description: A preceded B but did not necessarily cause B; intervention evidence vs correlation; mediators/confounders; identify unsupported causal step in multi-hop explanation.

title: Root-cause attribution
description: given symptoms/events and dependency graph, rank plausible root causes separately from downstream manifestations; include cases with insufficient evidence or multiple equally compatible causes.

title: Evidence provenance
description: given claims and source snippets, map each claim to supporting evidence; unsupported, directly supported, inferred, contradicted, or sourced from the wrong document.

title: Source reliability in-context
description: given explicit metadata such as primary record, repost, anonymous comment, official specification, outdated manual, decide which source is suitable for which claim without relying on source prestige alone.

title: Semantic similarity and factual correctness
description: does summary preserve source meaning? contradiction vs paraphrase; over-generalization; omitted qualifier; invented detail; unsupported certainty; incorrect entity/date/quantity.

title: Summary completeness
description: does summary cover all materially distinct topics? which topic is absent? does it spend disproportionate space on minor detail? distinguish concise-but-complete from lossy.

title: Claim entailment
description: source says “may reduce latency”; candidate says “reduces latency”: unsupported certainty. Source says 8–12%; candidate says 10%: approximation vs fabrication. Multi-sentence entailment and contradiction.

title: Unknown/known-state classification
description: given evidence set, distinguish true, false, likely, possible and genuinely unknown rather than guessing a binary answer.

title: Answerability from provided context
description: question may have a real-world answer but cannot be answered from supplied state; distinguish “unknown to the model state” from “factually unknowable” and “explicitly contradicted.”

title: Evidence sufficiency
description: is there enough evidence to make a requested decision at confidence threshold X? decide what additional evidence would discriminate between remaining alternatives.

title: Fact-vs-inference classification
description: identify statements explicitly present, deductively derivable, probabilistically inferred, merely plausible, or unsupported.

title: Hallucination detection
description: candidate response introduces person, date, dependency, number, cause, quotation, API, event or feature absent from source; include subtle composite hallucinations formed by combining true fragments.

title: Topic/keyword fidelity
description: do keywords describe the source? overly broad/narrow terms; missing dominant topic; term present only incidentally; rank keywords by representativeness.

title: Information-retrieval relevance
description: query plus 20–100 passages/items; rank relevance; distinguish exact lexical overlap from semantic relevance; IT/API/code/CSS/HTML/legal/scientific/general domains.

title: Recommendation/reranking quality
description: query, explicit preferences/constraints, candidate products/documents/actions/items; order by fit; hard constraint violation must dominate superficial similarity; ties and insufficient-information cases.

title: Entity resolution
description: are “International Business Machines”, “IBM Corp.” and “IBM” same entity in this context? distinguish same-name different entities using address/date/domain/account metadata.

title: Record deduplication
description: decide exact duplicate, near duplicate, updated record, related-but-distinct, or ambiguous using noisy text fields.

title: Cross-document reconciliation
description: invoice vs purchase order vs delivery note; resume vs application form; API docs vs implementation; identify matching, missing, contradictory and outdated facts.

title: Document consistency
description: invoice subtotal/tax/total agreement; stated address vs country code; account owner vs invoice party; dates in plausible order; internal references resolve.

title: Booking/accounting mapping
description: bank-statement descriptions → rent, payroll, cloud hosting, office equipment, tax, fee, refund, transfer, subscription etc.; debit/credit implications; recurring vs exceptional; business/private/unknown.

title: Accounting reasonableness
description: is booking category compatible with description? VAT treatment stated in supplied rules? asset vs expense under supplied threshold? candidate mapping clearly impossible or merely uncertain?

title: Invoice anomaly detection
description: implausible totals, duplicate positions, unusual quantity×price, inconsistent tax, dates, currencies, IBAN/country/address mismatch, changed payment destination.

title: Fraud/scam likelihood
description: emails, invoices, letters, account-change requests, fake support messages; German phone but unrelated foreign banking coordinates, domain typo, impossible chronology, urgency combined with credential/payment request; score individual evidence rather than “odd = fraud.”

title: Transaction anomaly detection
description: usual transaction pattern supplied in state; detect unusual amount, merchant, geography, frequency, timing or counterparty while tolerating legitimate one-off changes.

title: Commercial-price plausibility
description: given supplied catalogue/reference prices, judge invoice/order positions as plausible, unusually high/low, incompatible unit or quantity, or not comparable.

title: Budget consistency
description: proposed spend vs budget categories, recurring costs, commitments and reserve; identify oversubscription, double-counting or nominally cheap option causing downstream cost.

title: Resource planning
description: staff, compute, storage, inventory, time, materials, advertising budget; what is required, optional, excessive or missing; quantities under explicit workload assumptions.

title: Capacity planning
description: requests/s, workers, memory, storage growth, production capacity, hotel seats, warehouse space; choose sufficient capacity tier and detect impossible utilization assumptions.

title: Inventory decisions
description: demand forecasts, lead times, spoilage, safety stock; reorder/hold/clearance decisions; distinguish shortage risk from overstock risk.

title: Scheduling feasibility
description: jobs, dependencies, workers, durations, calendars; is schedule possible? earliest feasible slot? conflicting resources? missed prerequisite?

title: Prioritization under constraints
description: rank tasks using explicit impact, urgency, dependency, cost and deadline; reject “urgent-looking” low-value work when criteria disagree.

title: Pareto-optimal decision taking
description: multiple objectives such as latency/cost/accuracy/reliability; identify dominated options, Pareto frontier, and goal-compatible choices without pretending one global optimum exists.

title: Expected-utility decisions
description: explicit outcomes, probabilities and utility/cost; select or rank choices; include loss aversion traps, tiny-probability/high-cost events and cases where expected value differs from expected utility.

title: Bayesian evidence updating
description: prior plus diagnostic evidence/likelihood information; decide which hypothesis should gain/lose probability, rank posteriors, detect evidence that is actually non-informative.

title: Game-theory judgements
description: dominant strategies, best response, coordination, prisoner’s dilemma, zero/non-zero-sum, repeated interaction, credible threats, signaling; probable outcome under explicitly stated player incentives.

title: Adversarial-agent reasoning
description: another actor optimizes against you; identify exploitable deterministic strategy, deceptive signal, incentive incompatibility, commitment problem.

title: Negotiation judgements
description: BATNA, reservation values, mutually beneficial ranges, concessions; distinguish agreement that dominates alternatives from one that only sounds balanced.

title: Probability-support judgement
description: state gives probabilities/confidence/evidence; statement “it will probably be sunny in 3 days” must be evaluated against forecast values and uncertainty; distinguish 51%, 80%, 99% language.

title: Probability calibration language
description: map “possible”, “likely”, “very likely”, “almost certain” to supplied quantitative conventions; identify text whose certainty overstates/understates evidence.

title: Forecast consistency
description: multiple observations or forecasts through time; candidate prediction incompatible with current trajectory, confidence interval, seasonality or stated assumptions.

title: Counterfactual plausibility
description: given causal rules/state, judge “if X had not happened, Y would still have happened”; distinguish counterfactual inference from simple temporal reversal.

title: Base-rate awareness
description: rare event with noisy positive evidence; determine whether candidate conclusion ignores supplied prevalence/base rate.

title: Sampling/statistical interpretation
description: does a conclusion generalize beyond described sample? selection bias, survivorship, confounding, tiny sample, inappropriate average, percentage-vs-percentage-point confusion.

title: Unit understanding
description: compare quantities represented in different units; milliseconds vs seconds, MB vs GiB, km/h vs m/s, °C vs K when differences/absolute values matter, currencies with supplied conversion rates.

title: Dimensional consistency
description: is an equation/result dimensionally possible? energy vs power, rate vs amount, area vs length, throughput vs latency; detect numerically plausible but unit-invalid answers.

title: Order-of-magnitude reasoning
description: is result roughly 10, 1k, 1M or 1B? detect decimal/exponent/unit conversion mistakes without requiring exact arithmetic.

title: Scale plausibility
description: is 200 GB plausible for a text file containing 500 records? 2 ms plausible for a transatlantic round trip? grounded in explicitly provided reference ranges where possible.

title: Geometry and embodied navigation
description: textual 2D/3D spaces, orientation, coordinates, obstacles and goals; walk/drive/fly/jump/crawl constraints; choose feasible action and detect collision/dead end.

title: Spatial-relation reasoning
description: left/right/front/behind/inside/intersecting/north/south; viewpoint transformations; object A left of B and observer rotates 180°; relative vs absolute orientation.

title: Route feasibility
description: doors, one-way passages, bridge weight/height constraints, stairs vs wheelchair, vehicle turning radius, fuel/range; decide which route is actually traversable.

title: Embodied affordances
description: can object be carried, climbed, entered, opened, driven through, used as support given stated dimensions/material/body capabilities?

title: Physical commonsense
description: stack stability, containment, gravity, support, liquid flow, collision, friction, heating/cooling; plausible next physical state.

title: Mechanical-system reasoning
description: gears, pulleys, valves, pumps, levers, simple electrical/mechanical state descriptions; direction/change propagation and failure-mode classification.

title: Object permanence/state tracking
description: objects moved between locations/containers; after long distractor text identify where an object must, may or cannot be.

title: Temporal ordering
description: events with explicit/relative dates, durations and dependencies; detect impossible chronology, calculate which events overlap, before/after relations.

title: Calendar/time-zone understanding
description: appointments described across zones, daylight-saving offsets supplied or derivable from state, recurring schedules, “next Friday” relative to explicit reference date.

title: Historical-fact verification
description: given date/country plus reference excerpts, decide whether stated ruler, border, institution, technology, currency or event is compatible with that time.

title: Historical anachronism detection
description: objects, terminology, technologies, countries, institutions or social practices appearing before/after their described era.

title: Geographical consistency
description: city-country-region relationships, distances/directions from supplied map-like facts, impossible travel sequence, address-country/currency/phone-code consistency.

title: Weather-state interpretation
description: forecast table expressed textually; precipitation/cloud/wind/temperature state → supported natural-language judgement; distinguish “sunny”, “dry”, “warm”, “stormy”, “safe for activity X”.

title: Scientific-hypothesis plausibility
description: observations vs hypotheses; which hypotheses are consistent, falsified or underdetermined? distinguish prediction from post-hoc explanation.

title: Experimental-design judgement
description: does experiment test stated hypothesis? proper control? variable actually manipulated? confounder? measurement cannot distinguish candidate explanations?

title: Measurement/uncertainty reasoning
description: significant figures, measurement interval, sensor error, uncertainty propagation qualitatively, whether claimed difference exceeds supplied uncertainty.

title: Biological-system reasoning
description: text descriptions of cells, organisms, ecosystems, inheritance, physiology; identify plausible mechanisms, impossible category mixtures, cause/effect direction.

title: Biological signal understanding
description: symptom/body-state narratives → pain location/type/intensity range, physical vs psychological vs mixed vs insufficient evidence; explicitly reward uncertainty rather than invented sensations.

title: Medical differential-reasoning benchmarks
description: symptoms plus candidate ICD descriptions → score compatibility, contradiction and missing evidence; include superficially similar diagnoses, impossible combinations and insufficient-information cases; benchmark reasoning, not patient diagnosis.

title: Medical chronology consistency
description: symptoms, medication, procedures and measurements over time; decide whether candidate explanation contradicts chronology or known state supplied in example.

title: Translation correctness
description: source plus candidate translations; meaning preserved? polarity/tense/quantity/register changed? false friend? dropped clause? added information?

title: Grammar judgement
description: locate erroneous token/span among \~20 words; agreement, tense, case, article, word order, punctuation; include grammatically valid but stylistically odd distractors.

title: Glossary adherence
description: given N approved translations/technical terms, detect whether candidate translation uses required terms consistently; rank candidate glossary matches.

title: Synonym/semantic-substitution scoring
description: which word/phrase can replace source expression in context without changing denotation, connotation, register or technical meaning?

title: Word-sense disambiguation
description: “bank”, “port”, “model”, “class”, “cell”, “charge” etc.; determine intended sense from context and rank alternatives.

title: Language/dialect identification
description: short/noisy/code-switched text; language family vs exact language; distinguish German/Dutch, Serbian/Croatian/Bosnian, Russian/Ukrainian etc.; permit uncertain/ambiguous.

title: Code-switch understanding
description: sentence changes languages midstream; assign spans/language, preserve named entities/loan words, understand cross-language coreference.

title: Pragmatic-intent understanding
description: “Could you open the window?” literal ability question vs request; indirect refusals, implied requests, soft commitments, rhetorical questions.

title: Sarcasm and humor understanding
description: sarcasm, irony, understatement, absurdity, incongruity, callback, pun, garden-path joke; classify mechanism and whether literal interpretation differs from intended meaning.

title: Humor explanation correctness
description: given joke plus candidate explanations, rank explanations; reject explanations inventing a pun or cultural reference absent from text.

title: Mood/atmosphere understanding
description: cinematic/story descriptions → tense, calm, ominous, melancholic, joyful, uncanny etc.; distinguish environmental mood from character emotion.

title: Tone/register classification
description: formal, intimate, hostile, deferential, clinical, promotional, passive-aggressive, uncertain; intensity score; detect mismatch with intended audience.

title: Dialogue coherence
description: does response answer previous turn? wrong referent? repeats solved question? abrupt topic switch? ignores correction? assumes information never supplied?

title: Conversation-state tracking
description: multi-turn text with changing choices/reservations/configuration; identify latest valid state rather than an obsolete earlier value.

title: Persona consistency
description: persona explicitly specifies age, occupation, language, knowledge and experiences; candidate utterance contradicts biography, chronology or knowledge access.

title: Theory-of-mind / false-belief reasoning
description: Alice saw object moved? Bob did not; what does each person believe? nested beliefs, deception, stale information, private communication.

title: Embodied unknowns
description: what can this person/agent know given their location, sensors, messages, education and event exposure? reject omniscient answers.

title: Embodied time-aware world views
description: persona, age, birthplace, biography, explicitly supplied beliefs, media exposure and historical time; judge which beliefs/reactions are plausible for that described individual without substituting stereotypes.

title: Embodied emotions
description: baseline emotional/physical state plus new event → plausible next emotions; tooth pain + exhaustion + bad news vs rested state; allow multiple plausible reactions and reject deterministic overconfidence.

title: Emotion-cause attribution
description: identify which described event most plausibly caused emotion vs merely co-occurred; distinguish disappointment, fear, embarrassment, anger, grief, relief, surprise.

title: Social-norm reasoning
description: given explicit relationship/culture/context rules, classify action as expected, unusual, inappropriate or underdetermined; separate rule violation from personal dislike.

title: Relationship/permission reasoning
description: manager/employee, parent/child, owner/guest, doctor/patient, service roles as explicitly defined: who can authorize/access/change what?

title: Embodied animal understanding
description: species-specific state of dogs, cats, birds, fish, horses, rodents etc.; probable next action, stress/fear/feeding behavior, threat level, predator/prey relation, health concern vs normal behavior.

title: Animal affordance/constraint reasoning
description: can this species climb/swim/fly/squeeze through/open/reach the described object? age/size/injury/environment alter feasible actions.

title: Narrative next-event plausibility
description: given story state, rank candidate next events by causal continuity rather than genre cliché; impossible teleportation, forgotten injuries, unresolved physical constraints.

title: Character-goal consistency
description: does proposed action advance the character’s explicitly stated goal? knowingly sacrifices one objective for another? action conflicts with known incentives?

title: OCR/ngram-based text recognition
description: full document text plus focused sentence; tokenize into words/numbers and n-grams; identify customer number, invoice number, date, amount, reference, company/person/address from candidate spans.

title: Noisy-OCR reconstruction
description: `I/1/l`, `O/0`, broken whitespace, hyphenation, duplicated characters; rank candidate reconstruction using surrounding textual constraints.

title: Document-field association
description: multiple dates, IDs, addresses and amounts occur; determine which belongs to invoice, customer, supplier, delivery, payment or order rather than merely extracting nearest value.

title: Document-type classification
description: invoice, quote, reminder, order confirmation, cancellation, contract, bank statement, medical report, support ticket, shipping notice, application, receipt.

title: Document-workflow state
description: quote→order→delivery→invoice→payment→reminder; given documents/events, decide current state and which transitions have/have not happened.

title: Table reasoning from linearized text
description: rows/columns represented textually; lookup, compare, aggregate, identify max/min, join related rows, respect headers/units and missing cells.

title: Spreadsheet-formula semantics from text
description: formula plus cell values/ranges serialized textually; decide result/error/dependency; identify relative-reference mistakes without requiring spreadsheet modality.

title: Form completeness
description: required/conditional fields based on provided rules; missing signature, inconsistent checkbox/value, field supplied in wrong section, conditional field unnecessarily demanded.

title: Contract/clause consistency
description: given explicit contract clauses, decide whether proposed action/deadline/payment condition follows, conflicts, is unspecified or requires another clause; no free-form legal advice required.

title: Requirement traceability
description: requirements → design → implementation → tests; determine which requirement has no implementation/test, which test maps to no requirement, which artifact contradicts another.

title: Business-process conformance
description: defined workflow plus observed event sequence; legal transition, skipped approval, wrong role, duplicate action, expired prerequisite, valid exception path.

title: Email-thread state understanding
description: who owes whom a response? latest agreed date/price/action? question already answered? quoted older text vs newest message; attachment mentioned but absent.

title: Action-item extraction/verification
description: candidate action item actually promised/requested? correct owner/deadline? distinguish suggestion from commitment and condition from action.

title: Product/catalog matching
description: natural-language request vs structured product descriptions serialized as text; rank correct SKU/model while respecting size/version/compatibility constraints.

title: Compatibility matching
description: charger/device, software/plugin/runtime, replacement part/machine, datatype/API; distinguish physically similar from actually compatible.

title: Taxonomy/category assignment
description: assign products/documents/issues/scientific concepts to hierarchical labels; nearest category vs overly general/overly specific class.

title: Multi-label topic classification
description: text may genuinely belong to multiple domains; select all supported labels without spraying generic labels; include hierarchical and overlapping domains.

title: Domain identification
description: biology, chemistry, finance, networking, compiler engineering, law, linguistics, medicine, music, statistics etc.; score domain mixture rather than forcing one class.

title: Expertise-level estimation of text
description: introductory, practitioner, specialist/research-level based on concepts assumed and reasoning depth—not vocabulary complexity alone.

title: Explanation-necessity judgement
description: is answer self-evident from supplied context, or does decision materially benefit from justification? distinguish safety/ambiguity/high-impact decisions from simple lookups.

title: Explanation-quality judgement
description: given decision and rationale, does rationale actually support decision, merely restate it, introduce unrelated facts, reverse causality or use invalid evidence?

title: Rationale-to-answer consistency
description: model selects A but its explanation logically supports B; numeric reasoning disagrees with final label; cited evidence contradicts final answer.

title: Constraint-satisfaction judgement
description: candidate plan/output must obey many textual constraints: budget, size, dependency, date, allowed technologies, exclusions; identify exactly which constraints are violated.

title: Soft-vs-hard constraint discrimination
description: “must”, “prefer”, “ideally”, “unless”, “at most”, “around”; rank options without treating preferences as requirements or vice versa.

title: Preference learning from explicit examples
description: several accepted/rejected choices plus reasons; infer which candidate better matches demonstrated preference while distinguishing stable preference from incidental features.

title: Multi-criteria scoring consistency
description: given explicit scoring rubric, does stated total/category follow component scores? candidate may manipulate weighting, normalize incorrectly or ignore veto criteria.

title: Rubric-based quality assessment
description: article, support response, code review, product description, explanation; supplied rubric defines factuality/completeness/style/etc.; score dimensions separately rather than generic “good/bad.”

title: Comparative judgement transitivity
description: A preferred to B, B to C under same criterion; detect inconsistent candidate ranking unless supplied context legitimately changes criterion.

title: Pairwise preference prediction
description: two candidate outputs against explicit task/rubric; choose A/B/tie/insufficient evidence; useful primitive for reward/reranker training.

title: Set coverage / diversity judgement
description: does selected set cover required topics/categories rather than containing five near-duplicates? rank candidate subsets by relevance plus non-redundancy.

title: Redundancy detection
description: sentences, requirements, tests, retrieved documents, recommendations convey same semantic content despite different wording; exact vs partial redundancy.

title: Information-density judgement
description: candidate contains useful distinct information vs verbosity/repetition; important for deciding compression/summarization without treating all length as bad.

title: Data-quality validation
description: impossible ages/dates/ranges, inconsistent identifiers, duplicate IDs, unexpected missingness, categorical values outside domain, conflicting fields.

title: Synthetic-data plausibility
description: does generated record obey supplied distributions, dependencies and business rules? identify impossible combinations and suspicious template repetition.

title: Class-label leakage detection
description: training example contains target label or deterministic proxy in input; filename/category/template directly reveals gold decision.

title: Dataset-example quality
description: ambiguous gold label, multiple correct answers, unsupported rationale, malformed state, trivial lexical shortcut, answer leaked in prompt, wrong difficulty.

title: Benchmark-contamination clues
description: candidate task reproduces a supplied known example nearly verbatim vs legitimately same concept; n-gram/semantic overlap classifications from provided corpora.

title: Adversarial-example detection
description: irrelevant distractors, conflicting metadata, misleading lexical overlap, injected false premise; determine which evidence is actually decision-relevant.

title: Spurious-correlation resistance
description: training-style pattern says one label but causal/semantic evidence says another; names, formatting, length, position or irrelevant demographic-like attributes deliberately correlate with wrong answer.

title: Invariant detection
description: given examples/transitions/code/data, decide which property remains invariant; proposed operation preserves or breaks it.

title: Boundary-condition judgement
description: value exactly at min/max, zero, empty set, one-element collection, overflow threshold, inclusive/exclusive dates; determine which branch/rule applies.

title: Failure-mode classification
description: timeout, validation failure, authorization failure, dependency outage, resource exhaustion, logic bug, malformed input, user cancellation; infer from textual observations.

title: Recoverability judgement
description: retry, rollback, restart, compensate, request user input, permanent failure; classify based on supplied failure semantics.

title: Reversibility/destructiveness
description: actions/code/commands/business operations: reversible, compensatable, partially reversible, destructive; estimate blast radius from explicitly supplied resources.

title: Operational urgency
description: incident evidence → immediate intervention vs observe vs scheduled repair; based on explicit SLA/resource/error-rate thresholds rather than generic alarmism.

title: Change-risk judgement
description: small local refactor vs schema migration vs auth-system rewrite; score probable blast radius using dependency/state/test evidence, independent of code length.

title: Regression-likelihood judgement
description: changed module has many dependents, public contract change, no tests, state migration, or isolated internal refactor; rank patches by regression risk from provided evidence.

title: Human-vs-machine task suitability
description: given workflow requirements, classify deterministic automation, LLM-compatible judgment, requires external measurement, requires human authority, or hybrid verification.

title: Live-data requirement
description: can decision be made completely from supplied text/state, or does correctness require current database/network/sensor/time-dependent information?

title: Information-acquisition value
description: when state is insufficient, rank possible next questions/measurements by expected ability to disambiguate hypotheses rather than merely asking for more data.

title: Stopping/decision sufficiency
description: enough evidence already exists; gathering more data is unlikely to alter action vs decision should be deferred because critical uncertainty remains.

title: Confidence-vs-evidence consistency
description: answer may be correct but confidence unjustifiably high/low; score whether confidence follows amount/quality/consistency of supplied evidence.

title: Self-consistency across outputs
description: category says “safe”, score says 0.92 dangerous, rationale says destructive; detect contradictions among multiple typed outputs.

title: Granularity selection
description: question supports exact value, interval, category, ranking or only unknown; choose the strongest answer type justified by evidence rather than inventing precision.

title: Abstraction-level matching
description: question asks architecture-level issue but answer gives syntax detail; asks exact API but response gives generic concept; classify too abstract/appropriate/too specific.

title: Analogy validity
description: two systems share relevant structure vs superficial similarity; determine which properties transfer and where analogy breaks.

title: Category-error detection
description: treating latency as throughput, probability as confidence, class as instance, map as territory, correlation as cause, implementation as specification, price as value.

title: Cognitive-bias/illogic detection
description: base-rate neglect, sunk cost, conjunction fallacy, framing, survivorship bias, anchoring, denominator neglect, availability bias; identify the reasoning error without assuming every surprising choice is biased.

title: Contradiction-resolution
description: multiple claims disagree; determine whether genuinely contradictory, about different time periods/entities/scopes, or reconcilable through qualifiers.

title: Scope reasoning
description: “all users” vs “paid users”; “Europe” vs “EU”; “may” vs “will”; “under load” vs universally; detect candidate conclusions that silently broaden scope.

title: Quantifier reasoning in natural text
description: `all`, `none`, `some`, `at least one`, `exactly one`, `most`, `not every`; identify when paraphrase changes logical force without turning this into purely formal-logic tasks.

title: Negation/polarity tracking
description: nested negation, “not uncommon”, “fails unless”, “cannot exclude”, “only if”; determine actual proposition and catch polarity-flipped summaries/translations.

title: Reference/coreference resolution
description: which “it”, “they”, “former”, “latter”, “this version”, “that company” refers to; long technical/business documents with plausible distractors.

title: Comparative-language reasoning
description: “A is 20% faster than B”, “B takes 20% longer”, “no worse than”, “second highest”; decide candidate ordering and detect non-equivalent paraphrases.

title: Definition adherence
description: state explicitly defines a domain-specific term; later decision must use that local definition even if common usage differs.

title: Local-rule-over-world-knowledge judgement
description: synthetic world says red tokens are valid only on Tuesdays; model must follow supplied world state rather than pretrained associations.

title: World-model consistency
description: large textual state establishes entities/properties/rules; candidate event must respect all previous state, not just immediately preceding sentence.

title: Long-context distractor resistance
description: relevant fact appears far from query among semantically similar but irrelevant material; identify correct evidence without positional bias.

title: Needle-set retrieval
description: multiple separate facts across long state jointly determine answer; one fact alone suggests wrong answer; useful for testing distributed evidence integration.

title: Cross-domain synthesis
description: decision requires combining e.g. unit conversion + API constraint + budget, or geography + invoice metadata + chronology; individual subtasks easy, composition determines gold.

title: Minimal-sufficient-explanation selection
description: several explanations are true but some include unnecessary unsupported assumptions; select the explanation requiring the fewest additional assumptions while covering evidence.

title: Competing-hypothesis discrimination
description: multiple plausible explanations; identify observations that favor one, observations shared by all, and what new evidence would separate them.

title: Mechanism-vs-pattern distinction
description: data exhibits correlation/pattern, but proposed explanation claims a mechanism not established; score evidential support for mechanism separately from predictive usefulness.

title: Decision robustness
description: small plausible changes to uncertain inputs should or should not change chosen action; classify robust vs knife-edge decisions.

title: Sensitivity analysis
description: which parameter matters most to decision? e.g. cloud cost dominated by GPU hours rather than storage; ranking should change only when a threshold is crossed.

title: Dominated-information detection
description: new evidence is redundant because stronger evidence already implies it; useful for deciding whether an additional test/query has information value.

title: Consistency under paraphrase
description: same state/query expressed using alternate wording should yield same typed decision; detect lexical-position dependence.

title: Consistency under irrelevant-context insertion
description: add true but decision-irrelevant facts; answer should remain unchanged.

title: Consistency under option permutation
description: candidate options reordered or relabeled; output should follow semantics rather than positional preference.

title: Calibration under ambiguity
description: clean cases deserve high confidence, near-boundary or conflicting cases lower confidence; intentionally include cases where correct output is tie/null rather than forced class.

title: GPQA Diamond
description: GPQA Diamond is a benchmark for evaluating the reasoning capabilities of language models.
